_bob.plan: W8p, docs/COMFYUI.md track C, the shared processor the G7 grid is controlled with
_bob.purpose: Trellis2ProcessMesh over a mesh on disk: simplify to a face budget, drop floaters, weld and UV unwrap in one node, with the remesh branch the caller asks for. It is what puts a challenger model's raw output through the SAME processing the shipped one-shot route applies to its own.
_bob.derived_from: mesh_simplify_uv.json (W9c) for the load-and-export skeleton, with Trellis2ProcessMesh in place of Trellis2Simplify plus Trellis2UVUnwrap
deviations_from_source: Trellis2Simplify plus Trellis2UVUnwrap are replaced by the single Trellis2ProcessMesh, which is what W5t and W9b already carry. That is not a preference: G3b measured the two side by side on ten prompts and the pair leaves 1,467 to 3,050 boundary edges on a mesh that is supposed to be closed where the single node leaves 10 to 146. Processing a challenger's mesh through the pair would have scored W9c's sieve as the challenger's openness.

GeomPackNormalizeMeshToBBox(1.0) runs FIRST, and it is load-bearing twice over. Hunyuan returns a mesh spanning [-1, 1] where TRELLIS.2 returns [-0.5, 0.5], and Trellis2ProcessMesh does not normalise: measured at G7, an unnormalised challenger mesh lands at [-0.55, 0.55] after processing, which is outside the unit cube Trellis2EncodeMesh voxelises in, so W9t returns a fully BLACK albedo (in-chart std 0.0064, mean 0.0001 against 0.1810 and 0.3745 normalised). It also puts both models' meshes into ONE space before processing, so remesh_band, floater_threshold and weld_digits mean the same thing on both sides of the G7 grid.
remesh is a dynamic combo, so its sub-widgets belong to the selected branch and comfy.bind_process is what binds it. The shipped values here are the on branch, matching W5t and W9b.
_bob.requires_pack: ComfyUI-TRELLIS2 (PozzettiAndrea, MIT) plus its own hard requirement ComfyUI-GeometryPack (GPL-3.0), which W9t already needs
_bob.notes: No model is loaded, so the wall clock here is the algorithm rather than a checkpoint read, and it costs no VRAM of its own. Trellis2LoadMesh converts nothing on the way in and Trellis2ExportTrimesh turns the subject -90 degrees about X on the way out, so a file that has been through this graph has one more export to undo: see comfy.stage_exports.
